extracted.intended_audience: NAACL authors, reviewers, action editors, senior area chairs, and the NLP research community
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the review workflow, responsibilities, and evaluative requirements used to review and decide acceptances for NAACL-HLT 2022 submissions, including ARR commitments, ethics review, and special-theme handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reviewing requirement (ARR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions in the ACL Rolling Review received at least three reviews and one meta-review during the centralized rolling review phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ARR process was organized so every paper submitted received at least three reviews and a meta-review to provide authors with sufficient feedback before they decide to commit to a venue. Action editors and reviewers were coordinated to meet this requirement while balancing the reviewing load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step ARR → venue commitment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing and acceptance via ARR is a two-step process: (1) centralized rolling review where submissions receive reviews and meta-reviews, and (2) authors optionally commit the reviewed submission to a publication venue (e.g., NAACL), where SACs and Program Chairs make acceptance decisions based on ARR outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After ARR reviews and meta-reviews are available, authors choose whether to commit to NAACL. Once committed, SACs act on the ARR reviews/meta-reviews (and other inputs) to form acceptance recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAC acceptance recommendation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior Area Chairs make acceptance recommendations per area by taking into account the submission itself, (meta-)reviews, comments to SACs provided by the authors, and ethics reviews when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SACs integrate all available information (paper text, ARR reviews and meta-reviews, author responses/comments to SACs, and any ethics reviews) when producing area-level acceptance recommendations for Program Chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible NLP Research checklist compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were asked to follow the ACL code of ethics and to fill out the 'Responsible NLP Research' checklist at submission to encourage best practices in ethics and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The checklist is intended to prompt authors to document ethical and reproducibility-related aspects of their work. Reviewers were explicitly asked to consult the checklist when deciding whether a paper requires an in-depth ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review flagging and escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on input from reviewers and action editors, SACs flagged papers that required an in-depth ethics review; flagged papers were handled by a dedicated committee of ethics reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics chairs provided guidance and office hours to SACs to help decide when to escalate. Ethics reviews were produced by the ethics committee and then integrated into SACs' final acceptance recommendations and Program Chairs' decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special theme (Human-Centered NLP) submission expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special theme submissions were invited that address research questions meaningfully incorporating stakeholders in the design, development, and evaluation of NLP resources, models, and systems, particularly those that combine NLP and HCI perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given their interdisciplinary nature, theme papers were reviewed through a dedicated process by reviewers with expertise in both NLP and Human-Computer Interaction to ensure appropriate evaluation of stakeholder-centered work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for acceptance to 'Findings of ACL: NAACL 2022'
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers accepted to the Findings companion publication were those assessed by the program committee as solid work with sufficient substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings papers were judged as having sufficient substance to merit publication though perhaps not accepted to the main conference; they were given the option to be presented as posters during the main conference (many accepted this option).
